sentence: This project studies an early step in how cells build the dynein arm, the large motor that powers cilia movement.
This project builds an artificial intelligence tool that explains how it decides whether skin lesions in images are cancer, using the rule dermatologists use.
This project builds a model to predict areas in the US at risk for Japanese encephalitis virus.
This project studies how proteins called tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases control nerve regrowth and pain after nerve injury.
This project runs a cancer center that does research and tries to reduce the burden of cancer.
This project studies how outside factors work through inflammation and immune pathways to raise the risk of prostate cancer in some populations.
This project uses synchrotron imaging to map and measure how myelin breaks down in the brain in Alzheimer's disease.
This project coordinates research on type 1 diabetes so that discoveries can become ways to prevent or treat the disease.
This project compares how well different CRISPR gene editing formulations work when given to fluorescent reporter pigs.
This project uses lambda dynamics simulations to study how drug resistance and protein binding work, to help design small molecule and protein therapeutics.
This project engineers T cells to target a tumor antigen found at low levels in cancer.
This project tests whether individuals who quickly develop tolerance to alcohol effects are more likely to have problematic alcohol use.
This project develops peptide antivirals that block viral entry and spread from host to host.
This project studies the tissue structure and nerves of ligaments in the sacroiliac joint and how changes in them relate to pain.
This project identifies which RNA molecules are actively translated in nucleus accumbens neurons when rats are re-exposed to a cocaine cue.
This project studies a pathway that regulates mitochondrial biogenesis and looks for secreted factors that it regulates.
This project studies how environmental toxicants and defective repair lead to epigenome changes and genetic and epigenetic differences in tumors.
This project studies how the brain combines sounds from the two ears into one, a process called binaural fusion.
This project develops MRI methods at ultra-high field to map molecular and physiological properties of tissue.
This project uses wearable technologies to study how changes in maternal glucose affect fetal behavior and autonomic regulation during pregnancy.
